title: What a private company left on the record
label: The numbers
lede: Ouya never filed with the SEC and never published revenue, losses or the number of consoles it sold. What follows is every figure we could confirm: the Kickstarter page, the funding rounds as reported, what developers and the chief executive said about sales, and the game counter on the company’s own home page. The gaps are gaps in the record.

blocks.title: Money raised, as reported
blocks.subtitle: $ millions. Three disclosed sums. The venture debt that forced the sale was never disclosed.
blocks.source: Kickstarter: $8,596,474, rounded[^1]. Venture round led by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers[^8][^9]. Alibaba[^23][^24]. The three add up to about $33.6M (derived). Fortune reported that Ouya also borrowed from TriplePoint Capital and that the amount “must have been more than” the $10M from Alibaba; the figure itself is unknown.[^24]

blocks.body: How many Ouya consoles were sold is **unknown**. The company declined to give a number in July 2013[^14] and we found none in any later primary source. The only firm floor is the Kickstarter page: 58,224 backers chose a reward that included a console (derived).[^1] Unit figures that circulate online could not be traced to the company or to a tracker and are left out.
